name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,425

clue.text: Father in lodgings decorated walls

indicators.note: one word sitting in another means it is placed inside that word

blocks.note: a pad is informal for a place to live

explanation.surface: Dad spruces up the rented rooms by putting up wallpaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father' tempts you towards the usual English abbreviation; here it is the French word, and lodgings is informal.
explanation.definitionFit: Walls that have been hung with paper have been papered, a kind of interior decorating.

clue.text: A bird eaten by friend of father

indicators.note: what is eaten ends up inside the eater, so these words go within the next

explanation.surface: A bird is gobbled up by a pal of Dad's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'friend of father' reads as one phrase, but the definition is just 'of father'.
explanation.definitionFit: Paternal is the adjective describing anything relating to or inherited from a dad.

clue.text: Holy father's secretary has to wash up

definitions.note: possessive phrase standing for an adjective

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading the word from bottom to top

blocks.note: waves lap or wash against the shore

explanation.surface: The Pope's secretary is stuck doing the dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wash up' looks like doing the dishes; it is LAP turned upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Papal means belonging to the Pope, who is called the Holy Father.

clue.text: Rear one inside? It might make father more distant

definitions.text: It might make father more distant

indicators.note: the word for one is put inside the word for rear

blocks.note: to do with the rear end of the body

explanation.surface: A puzzling question about the behind, followed by something that pushes Dad away.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside RECTAL. The definition is a joke: said aloud in a British accent, 'father' sounds just like 'farther', which is more distant.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a spoken performance, and speaking the word father out loud makes it sound like farther.

clue.text: Daddy there is high and dry

indicators.note: someone high is intoxicated and muddled, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Dad is stranded, left high and dry.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'high and dry' hides the split: 'high' is the signal and 'dry' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with all its water removed is dehydrated, i.e. completely dry.

clue.text: Reckoned pop's in a rush

indicators.note: one word sitting in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: a rush is a reed-like marsh plant
to pop something somewhere is to put it there

explanation.surface: Dad is supposedly in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pop' looks like Dad and 'rush' like haste; they are 'put' and a waterside plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Reputed means generally believed or supposed to be so, much as reckoned does.

clue.text: Pick poppa up, having taken time out

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top
time is the letter t, and taking it out removes that letter

explanation.surface: Choose Dad to collect, after he has done his time inside.
explanation.walkthrough: PATER reads up as RETAP; dropping its T leaves REAP.
explanation.definitionFit: To reap a crop is to gather or harvest it, which is to pick it.

clue.text: Papa gets longer in jug

blocks.note: P is Papa in the NATO phonetic alphabet
one who longs, or itches, for something

explanation.surface: Dad is getting more elongated while trapped in a jug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'longer' reads as 'more long', but it is a person who longs: an itcher.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitcher is a large container with a handle and lip for pouring liquid.

clue.text: Supposed the old man raised a boy

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting a word up reads it from bottom to top

blocks.note: a title or address for a man
a boy's name, short for Edward

explanation.surface: Assumed Dad brought up a son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the old man' reads as Dad, and 'raised a boy' as parenting; both phrases must be split into smaller pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To have theorised something is to have proposed it as a hypothesis, i.e. supposed it.

clue.text: Father can start to go courting

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter only

explanation.surface: Dad is able to begin going out with someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a verb meaning is able; it is the metal container.
explanation.definitionFit: Dating means seeing someone romantically, which is the old-fashioned activity of courting.

clue.text: Starts to tire of pa's irritatingly childish question

indicators.note: the starts of the following words are their opening letters

blocks.note: the first letter of each of these five words

explanation.surface: Dad begins to grow weary of a child's annoying question.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the initials of the five words after 'Starts to' are used.
explanation.definitionFit: A question in the sense of a matter under discussion is a topic, as in 'the question of funding'.

clue.text: Fervent father thrashed English lieutenant

indicators.note: something thrashed is beaten about, so its letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A passionate dad gave an English army officer a beating.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartfelt feelings are deeply and sincerely felt, which is what fervent describes.

clue.text: Da and I are recently getting into claret

indicators.note: a word getting into another goes inside it

blocks.note: as in 'the late news', meaning recent

explanation.surface: Father and son have lately taken to red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the opening phrase: a father and his child are kin.
explanation.definitionFit: A dad and his child are family members, connected by blood, so they are related.

clue.text: Father only protects bird

indicators.note: the outer words shield the letters held between them

blocks.note: found across the join of these two words

explanation.surface: Only Dad looks after the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A heron is a long-legged wading fowl found by rivers and lakes.

clue.text: Office suppliers' sire sat, not stirring

definitions.note: the clue's apostrophe makes it possessive

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: The father of the office-supply business sat there motionless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not stirring' reads as one phrase meaning still; 'not' is part of the letters and 'stirring' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Stationers sell paper, pens and similar goods, supplying offices with what they need.

clue.text: Shock as pop falls oddly

indicators.note: oddly means taking the letters in odd-numbered places

blocks.note: first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters

explanation.surface: Dad tumbling in a strange way is shocking.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal someone is to horrify or dismay them greatly.

clue.text: Father takes Portuguese gents snacks

blocks.note: Dom is a Portuguese title for a gentleman

explanation.surface: Dad brings some Portuguese men along to nibble on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Portuguese' looks like P; the whole phrase is DOMS, from the Portuguese title Dom.
explanation.definitionFit: Poppadoms are thin crisp Indian flatbreads eaten as a snack or starter.

clue.text: During Question Time, retired father is a star!

indicators.note: retired means gone back, so the word is read backwards
one thing happening during another sits inside it

explanation.surface: A retired dad appears on the TV panel show Question Time and is a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: Question Time is a BBC political debate programme, but here the two words are split and used separately.
explanation.definitionFit: An asterisk is the small star-shaped symbol used in print; its name comes from Greek for little star.

clue.text: Firm dads keep quiet in police premises

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within

explanation.surface: Strict fathers stay silent inside the police station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like strict; it is a company. Cop shop is British slang for a police station.
explanation.definitionFit: Cop shops is slang for police stations, the buildings where officers are based.

clue.text: A quiet dad, maybe glaring

blocks.note: piano, the musical direction for quiet
a dad is one example of a parent

explanation.surface: A silent father, perhaps staring fiercely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'glaring' suggests staring angrily, but here it means obvious, as in a glaring error.
explanation.definitionFit: A glaring mistake is plainly visible, and apparent means clearly evident or obvious.

clue.text: Dada's wrong about last epilogues

indicators.note: letters gone wrong are out of their proper order
about means going round, so these letters surround another word

blocks.note: the last part is the end

explanation.surface: The Dada art movement was mistaken about its closing statements.
explanation.walkthrough: Dada was an early 20th-century art movement; here it is just four letters to rearrange around END.
explanation.definitionFit: Addenda are sections added at the end of a book, like epilogues.

clue.text: Call from father, travelling west, in Brazilian city

indicators.note: in an across entry, travelling west means moving right to left
one word in another goes inside it

explanation.surface: Dad phones home while on his way west in Rio.
explanation.definitionFit: To radio someone is to call or contact them by wireless transmission.

clue.text: Two notes about e.g. child with adoptive father reviewed and edited

indicators.note: viewed again from the other end, so the word is read backwards
about means going round another word

blocks.note: RE is a sol-fa note, and N is the abbreviation for note
a ward is a child in the care of a guardian

explanation.surface: Two memos about a foster child were looked over and amended.
explanation.walkthrough: The two notes split around the middle: RE before and N after. 'notes' looks like memos, not music and an abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Something redrawn has been drawn again with changes, so it has been edited or revised.

clue.text: Inspectors of son's father on TV

blocks.note: Father Ted, the Irish TV sitcom priest

explanation.surface: A TV inspection of a son's dad.
explanation.walkthrough: Ofsted is the government body that inspects schools in England; Father Ted was a 1990s sitcom about an Irish priest.
explanation.definitionFit: Ofsted is the official organisation whose inspectors assess schools and childcare in England.

clue.text: Swindling foreign woman gets close to dad

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A dishonest German woman cosies up to Dad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' looks like near; here it means the end of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Fraud is the noun for deception done for gain, which is swindling.

clue.text: So case closed - finally I discharge father's killer

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of each preceding word

blocks.note: the last letter of each of these three words
pus is a discharge from a wound

explanation.surface: A detective wraps up the case of who killed the father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' applies to all three words before it. In Greek myth, Oedipus unknowingly killed his father Laius.
explanation.definitionFit: Oedipus, the legendary Theban king, slew his own dad without knowing who he was.

clue.text: Father's Day, touching for father

explanation.surface: A sentimental Father's Day, standing in for Dad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father's Day' reads as the celebration; it is three separate pieces. The definition is a religious father.
explanation.definitionFit: A padre is a priest or chaplain, addressed as Father, especially in the armed forces.

clue.text: Pop rang his mum

indicators.note: to pop is to burst, breaking the word apart so its letters re-form

explanation.surface: Dad phoned his mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' does double duty: it signals the shuffle, and 'his' refers back to Pop, whose mum is the child's grandmother.
explanation.definitionFit: Dad's mother is the grandmother of his children, informally called Gran.

clue.text: May one fathered by Odin enter violently?

indicators.note: violent action throws things about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: the Norse thunder god was a son of Odin

explanation.surface: Is Odin's son allowed to burst in?
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' sits at the start as if asking permission, but it is the may tree, the hawthorn.
explanation.definitionFit: May is another name for hawthorn, a thorny tree that blooms in the month of May.

clue.text: I'll take over after dad waves goodbye

indicators.note: something that waves moves to and fro, so the letters are shifted about
after places the opening words second, behind the word for dad

blocks.note: I'll is 'I will', taking just the I
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: I'll step in once Dad has waved farewell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waves goodbye' reads as a phrase; 'waves' is the signal and 'goodbye' the definition. Addio is Italian for farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Addio is the Italian word for farewell, used in English as a parting word.

clue.text: After trial, is dad in contempt?

indicators.note: after a trial run the letters are set out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Following a court case, has Dad been held in contempt of court?
explanation.walkthrough: 'in contempt' looks like the legal phrase, but 'in' is one of the letters and 'contempt' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Disdain is a feeling of scorn for something judged unworthy, which is contempt.

clue.text: We hear no father to boys is gloomy

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

blocks.note: a man with no boys to be father to has no sons

explanation.surface: Apparently a man with no sons is a miserable one.
explanation.definitionFit: Without sunshine a place or day is dark and dull, so gloomy.
